title: Semantic-tiered fingerprinting and GPU-aware compacting for cross-request prefix reuse
creator: Michael Chen
description: Problem: We observe duplicated prefix computations and suboptimal slab packing across concurrent requests, causing avoidable GPU memory churn and higher per-token cost for multi-tenant workloads. Existing fingerprinting is exact-hash based and misses semantically similar prefixes that would benefit from shared KV entries. Goal: implement a semantic-tiered fingerprinting layer combined with a GPU-aware compaction pass that groups similar prefixes into shared, compact slabs and opportunistically spills low-value entries to host RAM when GPU pressure is high. This ticket covers design, prototype, and canary rollout of the feature.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Semantic fingerprinting returns candidate matches for >60% of repeated prefixes in production trace sample (vs ~35% baseline). 2) End-to-end benchmark shows >=10% reduction in GPU-resident KV size for mixed conversational workload while maintaining <2% change in response quality metrics (per prompt set). 3) No regression in p99 generation latency on dedicated pools (within 5% baseline). 4) Feature gated and canaryable via runtime feature flag; telemetry emits hit/miss/merge events and GPU memory delta per slab compaction.
design_decisions:
- Use a two-stage fingerprint: (a) a compact locality-sensitive hash (LSH) sketch emitted at tokenization time, and (b) a short canonicalized token prefix signature for exact verification. LSH provides candidate clusters; verification prevents false-positive merges.
- Maintain a three-tier cache: hot (GPU-resident exact entries), warm (packed GPU slabs of merged semantically similar entries), cold (host RAM compressed journal).
- Compaction runs asynchronously on a shard-level compactor thread; compaction policy is credit-driven: entries accrue 'reuse credits' via hits and decay over time. Low-credit entries are eligible to be compacted into shared slabs or evicted to cold tier.
- When GPU memory free falls below pressure_threshold (configurable), compactor increases spill aggressiveness and prefetch throttling.
- Verification mirrors existing KV read path: candidate->verify->either coalesce KV pointer or fallback to independent entry. This preserves correctness for exact-match semantics (important for stateful prompts).
implementation_notes:
- New components: lsh_fingerprint module (Rust), slab_compactor service, memory_orchestrator hooks to trigger spill.
- Storage change: add 'semantic_tag' metadata to KV ledger entries (8 bytes). Keep on-disk compatibility via versioned ledger header.
- Expose metrics: kv.semantic_candidate_count, kv.semantic_coalesce_rate, gpu.kv_resident_bytes_by_tier, slab_compaction_duration_seconds.
- Toggle via feature flag 'kv_semantic_compaction_v1' at request-routing layer. Canary uses per-customer header routing to dedicated canary pool.
- Unit tests: deterministic LSH with seeded RNG, compaction invariants, verification false-positive/negative bounds.
- Perf harness: reuse existing batching trace replay with 1M requests sampled from prod week of 2026-01-20.
benchmarks: Preliminary local-run on a 4xA100 simulation: semantic candidate recall 0.62 on sampled trace; coalesce_rate 0.28; GPU-resident KV bytes reduced by 12% after steady-state compaction. Latency p99 increased by 1.9% in worst-case with verification enabled; with verification optimized via fast-path cache, p99 impact reduced to <1%. Quality evals on internal prompt set showed BLEU-style similarity delta <0.8% and destination-entity extraction equal within noise. Detailed numbers and CSVs are in the linked experiment notebook.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branch behind feature flag and run full unit/integration tests. 2) Internal perf run on staging cluster with production trace (run for 48h). 3) Canary rollout to 5% of infra and two low-risk customers for 72h. Monitor kv.semantic_coalesce_rate, gpu.kv_resident_bytes_by_tier, trace quality, and errors. 4) If metrics stable, increase to 25% and then 100% within two weeks with gradual config tuning. 5) Postmortem and tuning iteration after full rollout.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: False-positive merges could change outputs for prompts relying on tokenization edge-cases. Mitigation: require exact verification before coalescing; start with conservative LSH radius.
- Risk: Compaction CPU overhead impacting request throughput. Mitigation: compactor runs async with backpressure and CPU budget; metrics to surface compaction CPU usage per shard.
- Risk: Increased complexity in debugging. Mitigation: emit traceable events and tie slab ids to trace ids in debug builds; add quick un-merge tool for replay.
